MEMBER.NAME: words_xpp_readable
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Words 0xC0-0x1FF (bytes 0x180-0x3FF). XOR\'d by eeprom_verify_xor_checksum(). Readable via XPP Tag 0x86 (words 0x00-0xFF) and Tag 0x87 (words 0x100-0x1FF). xpp_flash_read_wrapper() hard-limits reads to 0x400 bytes from offset 0.

MEMBER.NAME: words_xpp_unreachable
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Words 0x200-0x3FF (bytes 0x400-0x7FE). XOR\'d by eeprom_verify_xor_checksum() BUT beyond 0x400-byte XPP read limit. Tags 0x88/0x89 return 0xFF fill. Only via TFTP ee_ar531x.dat (NML_bin.c:3096). LAST word 0x3FF (bytes 0x7FE-0x7FF) is checksum word: XOR(words 0xC0..0x3FF) must == 0xFFFF.

COMMENTS.COMMENT:
XPP_Establish_Secure_Identity_Link [Tag 0x81 handler -- registers Xbox MAC as trusted peer]
param: p_mac_addr -- 6-byte MAC address from Tag 0x81 payload in Type 0x07 CONNECT_REQ
Flow (spinlock protected): 1. Net_Init_Socket_Logic(p_mac_addr, 6) -- validates and registers MAC 2. If success: NET_Register_Peer_MAC(p_mac_addr) -- stores as trusted peer MAC 3. Sets g_XPP_Current_Session_ID = XPP_Get_Identity_Token() -- starts new auth session
WARNING: Once paired, adapter only responds to this MAC. Setting an incorrect MAC can soft-brick the adapter if you cannot send from the paired address to clear it. Use Tag 0x82 (Interface Reset) with a non-zero value to undo MAC spoofing and restore the hardware MAC via NET_Reinit_Interface_With_MAC().

TFTP_Open_Port69_Socket Opens UDP socket on port 0x45 (69) and registers g_XPP_Active_Frequency as the callback. This is the UNPAIRED port — no auth on WRQ, no auth on RRQ. Any host that has completed a valid XPP handshake can flash firmware through this port. Called from xpp_sync_radio_state() at boot. Gate: g_XPP_Session_Handle must be -1.

xpp_check_firmware_update_status [Boot init: opens both TFTP sockets]
Called from net_main_task() as a fixed step during boot, before DHCP, before any Xbox connection. Opens both TFTP listening sockets: TFTP_Open_Port16932_Socket(XPP_Secure_Config_Update, xpp_tftp_commit_config) Port 16932 = paired port, MAC+HMAC auth on WRQ, no auth on RRQ. TFTP_Open_Port69_Socket(0, TFTP_VFS_WRQ_Completion_Callback) Port 69 = unpaired port, no auth on WRQ or RRQ.
Both sockets open at power-on but transfers are gated by g_XPP_Session_Handle == -1. Gate is set by TFTP_Session_Enable() during the Type 0x01/0x02 handshake. Without a prior successful XPP handshake, both ports respond with "Transfers currently disabled".

TFTP_Session_Enable Sets g_XPP_Session_Handle = -1 (0xFFFFFFFF). Called during the XPP Type 0x01/0x02 handshake flow to gate-open both TFTP ports. Without this call any WRQ or RRQ on either port receives "Transfers currently disabled".

TFTP_Session_Disable Sets g_XPP_Session_Handle = 0 (cleared). Called on XPP session teardown / watchdog timeout to close the TFTP gate. Any in-progress transfers receive no further service after this is called.

TFTP_Process_New_Request Main entry point for all incoming WRQ/RRQ packets on both port 69 and port 16932. param_4 == 0 -> port 69 path (no auth, g_XPP_Active_Frequency callback) param_4 == 1 -> port 16932 path (XPP_Secure_Config_Update auth callback)
Flow: 1. Rejects if g_TFTP_Session_Active_Flag >= 1 (one session at a time). 2. Validates opcode < 3 (1=RRQ, 2=WRQ only). 3. For port 16932: filename field starts at p_tftp_opcode+0x3d (binary auth blob, not text). For port 69: filename is a null-terminated string starting at p_tftp_opcode+2. 4. Lowercases the mode string. 5. Allocates TFTP_Transfer_State via TFTP_Session_Alloc (pool tag 0x18, 0x80 bytes). 6. Sets port_source_id: 0x45 (port 69) or 0x4224 (port 16932). 7. Checks g_XPP_Session_Handle == -1, else sends "Transfers currently disabled". 8. Dispatches auth callback — for RRQ on port 16932: callback returns immediately (no checks). For WRQ on port 16932: MAC check then HMAC-SHA1 check. auth fail return -1 -> "Access violation", return -2 -> silent drop. 9. Allocates ephemeral TID UDP socket via xpp_udp_open_or_bind_socket(). 10. RRQ: sets state=6 (SEND), block=1, opens VFS file, callback = g_XPP_Link_Quality. WRQ: sets state=1 (RECV), sends ACK block 0 immediately (RFC 1350), callback = g_XPP_Security_State.
State values written at offset 0x38 (state_flags_lo): 1 = RECV (WRQ - waiting for DATA blocks) 6 = SEND (RRQ - sending DATA blocks) 2 = SEND_RRQ (RRQ initial state before first block sent)

TFTP_Session_Alloc Allocates a TFTP_Transfer_State descriptor from the network buffer pool. Pool tag: 0x18, size: 0x80 bytes. On success: increments g_TFTP_Session_Active_Flag, pushes onto g_UDP_Session_List_Head linked list, initialises retry fields: puVar1[0x1a] = 5 (initial retry interval, clamped [10, 150] ticks) puVar1[0x19] = 5 (retry counter initial value) puVar1[0x1e] = 1 (session active flag) Returns NULL on alloc failure — caller logs STR_tftp_alloc_fail.

TFTP_Session_Free Releases a TFTP_Transfer_State descriptor back to the buffer pool. Decrements g_TFTP_Session_Active_Flag. Removes the descriptor from the g_UDP_Session_List_Head linked list. Called on: auth failure, session completion, error, or timeout exhaustion.

xpp_tftp_process_ack *** BUG: BLOCK COUNTER NEVER ADVANCES ON RRQ ***
This function handles incoming ACK packets from the client during RRQ (read/send) sessions.
THE BUG - two separate problems that compound each other:
PROBLEM 1 - Wrong field used for block number comparison: The ACK block number from the wire is read from: *(short *)(*(int *)(p_protocol_state + 0xc) + 2) This is: *(p_session->vfs_filename_ptr + 2) i.e. bytes 2-3 of the VFS FILENAME STRING, not any packet buffer. The filename pointer at 0x08 is being read as if it were a packet buffer pointer. This means the "received block number" is always two bytes into the filename string ("ma" for mac.dat, "r5" for ar5eepo.dat etc.) — garbage, never matching.
PROBLEM 2 - Block counter increment is AFTER the branch: *(short *)(p_protocol_state + 0x2c) = *(short *)(p_protocol_state + 0x2c) + 1 This line only executes if the block number comparison PASSES. Since the comparison always fails (Problem 1), next_expected_block NEVER increments.
RESULT: Every ACK received is treated as out-of-sequence: param_1->out_of_seq_count++ (the else branch always fires) State stays at 2 (SEND), xpp_tftp_send_data_block re-sends block 1 forever. Client gets the same block on every retry until retry_limit_countdown hits zero and the session is torn down with a timeout error.
WHY FIRMWARE FLASH WORKS: WRQ (write) path goes through xpp_tftp_data_handler, NOT this function. xpp_tftp_data_handler correctly reads the block number from param_2 (actual packet buffer pointer) and correctly increments next_expected_block on success. The bug is 100% isolated to the RRQ ACK handler.
AFFECTED FILES (all RRQ reads broken): dbgout.txt, ar5eepo.dat, ar5maco.dat, image (read-back)
UNAFFECTED: WRQ firmware flash (xpp_tftp_data_handler - correct implementation) WRQ virtual file writes (TFTP_VFS_WRQ_Completion_Callback - correct)
CORRECT IMPLEMENTATION SHOULD BE: *(short *)(*(int *)(p_protocol_state + 0x18) + 2) // packet buffer at 0x18 not: *(short *)(*(int *)(p_protocol_state + 0x0c) + 2) // filename ptr at 0x0c

BUG ROOT: addiu v1,s0,0xC -- offset 0x0C = client_ip field (WRONG) CORRECT OFFSET SHOULD BE: 0x04 = ephemeral socket handle (p_tx_packet_buf) Patch bytes at 800030b8: 2463 000C -> 2463 0004 The ACK packet block number must be read from the ephemeral socket TX buffer, same way xpp_tftp_data_handler reads from param_2 (the incoming packet buffer). xpp_tftp_process_ack receives no packet buffer pointer in its arguments at all -- that is the second part of the bug: the ACK packet reference is not passed in.

*** BUG *** Wrong offset: 0x0c = vfs_filename_ptr, should be 0x18 = p_rx_packet_buf. This loads 2 bytes from inside the filename string instead of from the received ACK packet. The comparison below always fails. Block 1 repeats until timeout. FIX: change addiu offset to 0x18.
BUG: dereferences filename ptr as if it were a packet buffer - reads 2 bytes into filename string
BUG: v1 = *(filename_string + 2) e.g. "r5" for ar5eepo, "c." for mac.dat - never matches wire ACK block num
t9 = next_expected_block (currently 1 on first send, never advances)
BUG: comparison always FAILS - falls to out_of_seq path. Block 1 is retransmitted forever.
out_of_seq_count++ -- always fires because comparison above always fails
next_expected_block++ -- CORRECT but unreachable due to bug at 800030c8

xpp_signal_data_ready -- TFTP packet dispatcher (routes incoming packets to correct handler) Called when a UDP packet arrives on an active TFTP session socket.
Reads opcode from wire packet: *(short*)(session+0x0C dereference)+0 -> opcode opcode 3 (DATA) -> xpp_tftp_data_handler (WRQ receive path -- WORKS CORRECTLY) opcode 4 (ACK) -> xpp_tftp_process_ack (RRQ send path -- BROKEN, see below) opcode 5 (ERROR) -> xpp_tftp_handle_remote_error
NOTE -- the ACK dispatch at 80003200 passes ONLY a0=p_session to xpp_tftp_process_ack. The actual received packet buffer (t8, loaded at 8000315c from session+0x10) is in a2 for the DATA handler call (800031ec) but is NOT passed at 80003200 for the ACK call. This is the ROOT CAUSE of the RRQ bug -- xpp_tftp_process_ack receives no pointer to the incoming ACK packet and therefore cannot read the wire block number from it. It then reads from session+0x0C instead, which is garbage (client_ip field).
FIX at 80003200: change to or a2,t8,zero before the jal (pass t8 as param_2) AND fix xpp_tftp_process_ack to use param_2 instead of session+0x0C.
t8 = packet buffer pointer (from session+0x10) -- passed to DATA handler but NOT to ACK handler
DATA dispatch -- CORRECT: a0=session, a2=t8 (packet buffer) passed to xpp_tftp_data_handler
ACK dispatch -- BUG: t8 (packet buffer) not passed to xpp_tftp_process_ack
BUG: jal xpp_tftp_process_ack with only a0=session, a2 is NOT set (packet buf t8 dropped)

XPP_Packet_Dispatcher_And_Checksum_Validator *** MISNAMED in original analysis -- this is the FULL XPP packet dispatcher, not just echo ***
Entry point for all inbound XPP packets after EtherType 0x886F is confirmed. Validates RFC 1071 checksum over the XPP payload. Failure -> silent drop, no response.
Full dispatch table (from decompile, all paths confirmed): Tag 0x00 -> xpp_udp_handle_TYPE_00_Echo Sends 60-byte all-zeros response (no XPP magic, no checksum). Increments g_CNT_XPP_DISCOVERY_RECV counter. Tag 0x03 -> xpp_handle_TYPE_03_StatusQuery Increments g_CNT_XPP_IN_ERRORS (misnamed counter -- this is Type 0x03 scan req). Tag 0x04 -> silent drop + packet free. Increments g_CNT_XPP_TYPE_04. Tag 0x05 -> silent drop + packet free. Increments g_CNT_XPP_TYPE_05. Tag 0x08 -> Smurf/loop detection then XPP ICMP-style echo reply (Type 0x08). Checks dst IP against own IP / broadcast / multicast before reflecting. Smurf detected -> net_log_security_alert(0x10, MSG_Smurf_Attack_Detect). Valid -> reflects packet, increments g_XPP_PAYLOAD_LIMIT_256. Tag 0x0B -> silent drop + packet free. Increments g_CNT_XPP_TYPE_0B. Tag 0x0C -> silent drop + packet free. Increments g_CNT_XPP_TYPE_0C. Tag 0x0D -> XPP discovery/ping reply (14 bytes, Len_Dwords=0x0E). Increments g_CNT_XPP_DISCOVERY_SENT and g_CNT_XPP_DISCOVERY_RECV. Tag 0x0F -> silent drop, no counter. default -> silent drop + packet free (unknown tag).
NOTE: Tags 0x01/0x07/0x09 (Handshake/FlashConfig/BeaconReq) are NOT dispatched here. Those are handled by the higher-level XPP_Ethernet_Dispatcher at 0x80003B20 which calls this function only for the subset above. The full XPP type dispatch is split across both functions.

XPP_Ethernet_Dispatcher [Top-level EtherType 0x886F packet dispatcher]
Called from the main network RX path when EtherType == 0x886F (NLB/XPP). Validates XPP magic (0x58424F58 'XBOX'), version bytes, and RFC1071 checksum. Checksum failure: silent drop, no response. Dispatches on Tag byte to individual type handlers: 0x00 -> XPP_Send_Type00_Reply (ECHO -- sends 60-byte all-zeros response) 0x01 -> XPP_Type02_0x01_Handshake 0x03 -> XPP_Type02_0x03_WifiScan 0x05 -> XPP_Type02_Build_AdapterInfo_Response 0x07 -> XPP_Type02_0x07_FlashConfig 0x09 -> XPP_Type02_0x09_QueryStatus 0x0B -> silent drop, internal counter++ 0x0C -> silent drop, internal counter++ 0x0F -> silent drop, no log, no counter other-> STUB_Stooges_Error_Handler: prints "Hey Moe, it dont woik. NYUK NYUK NYUK NYUK"

NET_Submit_Packet_And_Release_Lock [Submits packet to TX queue then releases mgmt + driver locks]
Calls NET_Submit_Packet_To_TX_Queue() then: net_mgmt_unlock_dispatch(0, ...) os_release_driver_lock()
The auto-generated Ghidra comment on xpp_calculate_checksum (now NET_Submit_Packet_To_TX_Queue) states: "Result will be bitwise NOT'd (~) before transmission. This is not a standard protocol." This refers to the XPP RFC1071 checksum being complemented before writing to XPP header bytes 10-11. Standard RFC1071 already produces the one's complement -- the additional NOT seen in the Ghidra decompile artifact is a decompiler misread of the MIPS NOR/NOT instruction sequence. The actual wire checksum IS standard RFC1071 (verified against wire captures).

XPP_Global_Poll_Interfaces [Three-priority interface polling loop]
Polls all registered socket descriptors across three priority levels. Each level has a slot array at param_1 + (level * 0x34).
Priority mapping: level 0 -> iVar4 = 1 (high -- XPP management sockets) level 1 -> iVar4 = 2 (medium -- WLAN data path) level 2 -> iVar4 = 0 (low -- background / serial CLI / BBN discovery)
For each socket in each level: NET_Control_Logic_Dispatcher(socket, priority_code, param_3, param_4) Non-zero return -> xpp_register_active_socket(socket, &active_set[level])
OS_Lock_Global() held for the entire call. Active socket set passed back to main network task for dispatch. Exits via __common_exit_s0_s8() (MIPS callee-save restore + return).

NET_Pool_Dequeue_Packet_Descriptor [Pops the head node from a pool queue, updates depth and low-water mark]
param_1 = pool queue struct ptr (int*): [0] = head node ptr [1] = tail node ptr [2] = current depth [4] = low-water mark (min depth seen)
Flow: piVar1 = *param_1 (head) if NULL: return NULL (pool exhausted) *param_1 = *piVar1 (head = head->next) *piVar1 = 0 (clear dequeued node next ptr) if *param_1 == 0: param_1[1] = 0 (tail = NULL if queue now empty) param_1[2]-- (depth--) if param_1[4] > depth: param_1[4] = depth (update lwm) return piVar1
The low-water mark at [4] tracks pool exhaustion events. Pool exhaustion -> NULL return -> silent drop or firmware crash depending on caller. g_POOL_SMALL_PACKETS exhaustion is the most common cause of dropped XPP management frames under load.

NET_TXQ_Append_And_Update_Hwm [Appends a node to a queue and updates high-water mark]
param_1 = queue head struct ptr (int*): [0] = head node ptr [1] = tail node ptr [2] = current depth (count) [3] = high-water mark (max depth seen) param_2 = node to append (undefined4*)
Flow: *param_2 = 0 (clear node next ptr) if queue empty (*param_1 == 0): *param_1 = param_2 (head = node) else: *(tail) = param_2 (link to current tail) param_1[1] = param_2 (tail = node) param_1[2]++ (depth++) if param_1[3] < depth: param_1[3] = depth (update hwm)
Used for g_XPP_Transmit_Queue, g_POOL_LARGE_PACKETS, g_POOL_MEDIUM_PACKETS, g_POOL_SMALL_PACKETS, and g_XPP_Free_Descriptor_Queue. The high-water mark at [3] is readable via the CLI stats command.

NET_Pool_Alloc_Packet_Descriptor [Allocates a packet descriptor from the correct pool by size]
param_1 = requested data size in bytes
Pool selection logic: param_1 > DAT_800c01c4 (absolute max) -> return NULL (reject oversized) param_1 > g_NET_Max_Buffer_Size OR (g_WLAN_ADAPTER_STATUS==0 AND DAT_800cefd0==0) -> NET_Pool_Dequeue_Packet_Descriptor(&g_POOL_LARGE_PACKETS) param_1 > DAT_800c01b4 OR DAT_800cefd0==0 -> NET_Pool_Dequeue_Packet_Descriptor(&g_POOL_MEDIUM_PACKETS) else -> NET_Pool_Dequeue_Packet_Descriptor(&g_POOL_SMALL_PACKETS)
On success, initialises descriptor fields: [4] = [2] + 0x18 (payload_ptr = base + 24-byte descriptor header offset) [5] = 0 (payload_len = 0) [7] = 0 (flags = 0) [0xB] = 0 (type = 0) [1] = 0 (p_next = NULL) [10] = 1 (refcount = 1)
Three pool sizes (thresholds from g_NET_Max_Buffer_Size and DAT_800c01b4): Small: <= ~256 bytes (typical XPP management frames) Medium: <= ~1500 bytes (typical 802.11 data frames) Large: <= DAT_800c01c4 (firmware update blocks, EEPROM reads)

http_server_listener [TCP accept loop -- handles one HTTP connection per call]
param_1 = port (0x41E4 = 16868) param_2 = local IP (from g_XBOX_WIFI_IFACE+0x24) param_3 = HTTP_Connection state block (DAT_800cf6ac, 0x1696C bytes)
Flow: memset(param_3, 0, 0x1696C) -- zero entire connection state NET_Create_Protocol_Session(AF_INET=2, SOCK_STREAM=1, 0) -- create TCP socket setsockopt SO_REUSEADDR=1 bind(socket, {AF_INET, port, local_ip}) -- bind to port 16868 listen(socket, backlog=2) -- mark as passive listener
Accept loop: net_recv_packet() -- blocking accept, returns new client socket if accept fails: close listener, return http_request_parse_main(param_3) -- handle one HTTP request loops back to accept
One connection served at a time. After http_request_parse_main returns, the client socket is closed and the next connection is accepted. os_release_driver_lock() always called on exit regardless of error path.

http_request_parse_main [HTTP/1.x request parser -- reads headers and dispatches]
Parses one complete HTTP request from param_1->udp_socket_handle. 500ms read timeout per chunk (xpp_session_execute_sync timeout param).
Header fields parsed: Authorization: -> p_auth_header (pointer into rx_buffer, past "Authorization: ") Content-Length: -> content_length (integer) Content-Type: -> p_body_start, detects "multipart/form-data; boundary=" -> p_content_type_end If-Modified-Since:-> p_host_header (note: field named p_host_header but stores IMS value)
Methods supported: GET -> http_method = 1 HEAD -> http_method = 2 POST -> http_method = 3 other-> 501 Not Implemented
Path security: Must start with "/" Path traversal guard: rejects ".." segments FS_Normalize_Path() called to canonicalise "/" alone redirected to DAT_800c0274 (default page, likely "index.htm")
After parsing: http_uri_dispatcher(param_1, p_method_end) On any error: http_send_error_response then returns (no loop).

http_uri_dispatcher [Auth check + response builder + send]
Called after http_request_dispatch() populates p_get_handler / p_post_handler.
Flow: 1. http_request_dispatch() -- look up handler (sets request_type and handler ptrs) request_type == 0: no handler found -> 404 Not Found -> return 2. http_authenticate_request() -- Basic auth check Fails: 401 Unauthorized with WWW-Authenticate header -> return 3. Dispatch by request_type: type 2 (CGI upload): http_handle_post_upload() type 3 (POST form): get handler fn ptrs, call pfn_post_completion type 4 (XML GET): http_process_form_option_attributes() then send buffer type 1 (static GET): If-Modified-Since check -> 304 Not Modified if match else send static file content from handler buffer 4. HTTP_Send_Response_Headers(200, "OK") if response not already sent 5. http_udp_send_to_server() -- flush response headers 6. Send body in 0x578 (1400 byte) chunks via udp_send_to_server() 7. WLAN_Terminate_Discovery_Session() -- close client socket
NOTE: Function ends with os_check_stack_canary() -- does NOT return normally. Stack canary check is the exit point. This is intentional -- stack depth here is significant given the 0x1696C connection state block on the stack.

http_authenticate_request [HTTP Basic Auth validator against credential table]
Reads Authorization header from param_1->p_auth_header. Decodes base64 "Basic <base64(user:pass)>" credential. Splits on ":" to get username and password.
Credential table at DAT_800cf684 (runtime populated from NVRAM): Each entry is 0x28 (40) bytes: [+0x00] username (17 bytes max) -- from G_XPP_Identity_Password default "admin" [+0x11] password (17 bytes max) -- from g_NVRAM_User_Settings.Legacy_Padding default "admin" [+0x24] auth_level (4 bytes) -- access level for this credential
Count of entries: DAT_800bff44
Match logic: username empty OR username matches -> check password password matches -> check auth_level auth_level == -1 (no restriction) -> grant auth_level == handler required level -> grant else -> fall through to 401
Auth level from handler table: request_type 1 (GET): level from p_get_handler+0x14 request_type 4 (XML): level from p_get_handler+0x14 request_type 3 (POST): level from p_post_handler+0x10 level == -2: no auth required (public page)
On failure: http_send_401_unauthorized() with WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm=... Default credentials: admin:admin (both from NVRAM defaults "admin"/"admin") Can be changed via XPP Tag 0x03 (password only) or HTTP web UI (both fields).

HTTP_Send_Response_Headers [Builds and enqueues HTTP response header lines]
Builds the response preamble into param_1->tx_buffer via http_session_enqueue_data.
Headers always sent: "HTTP/1.x <status_code> <status_text>
" "Server: MN-740/<fw_version_string>
" (uses DAT_Firmware_Build_Date_String) "Connection: close
"
Optional headers (when non-NULL / non-zero): param_4 != 0: "Location: <param_4>
" (redirect URL) in_t0 != 0: "Content-Type: <in_t0>
" (MIME type string) response_status_code >= 0: "Content-Length: <len>
" (body size) in_t2 != 0: "Last-Modified: <in_t2>
" (cache header)
Status codes used by the firmware: 200 -> "OK" 304 -> "Not Modified" 400 -> "Bad Request" 401 -> "Unauthorized" (with WWW-Authenticate header added by http_send_401_unauthorized) 404 -> "Not Found" 501 -> "Not Implemented"
Server header value: "MN-740 <fw_version>" -- exposes firmware version to any HTTP client.

http_handle_post_upload [HTTP POST body receiver -- handles both raw and multipart uploads]
Shares g_HTTP_UPLOAD_BUFFER (1MB at 0x8024E4D0) with TFTP upload path. Maximum receive size: 0x100400 bytes (1049600, slightly over 1MB). Buffer cursor: G_UPLOAD_CURSOR tracks bytes received so far.
TWO UPLOAD MODES detected by p_content_type_end:
MODE 1 -- Raw POST body (p_content_type_end == NULL, no multipart): Copies rx_buffer remainder into g_HTTP_UPLOAD_BUFFER Reads remaining content_length bytes via xpp_session_execute_sync Sets p_query_string to g_HTTP_UPLOAD_BUFFER + DAT_800bff48
MODE 2 -- Multipart form data (p_content_type_end != NULL, has boundary): Reads all data until \r\n or \r\r\n\n terminator OR content_length reached Scans parts for "filename=" attribute to identify the file field If no filename found: error path If filename found: reads remaining bytes up to 1MB buffer limit Searches for MIME boundary marker (--boundary) to find end of payload Extracts payload from boundary-delimited region into g_HTTP_UPLOAD_BUFFER payload_length = end_boundary_offset - start_of_file_data
After receiving complete payload: param_1->p_upload_buffer = &g_HTTP_UPLOAD_BUFFER param_1->upload_payload_len = payload_length Calls (*pfn_post_completion)(param_1) -- the registered POST completion handler
Completion handlers: /cgi/config.cgi -> http_apply_config_save_and_redirect (save config, reboot) /cgi/firmware.cgi-> xpp_tftp_commit_config equivalent (flash firmware, reboot if 1MB)
Ends with os_check_stack_canary() -- does not return normally.

http_server_task_main_loop *** NEVER CALLED -- task not launched in production firmware ***
THE BUG: cfg_http_firmware_upload_setup() at 0x80016598 IS the launch function for this task. It calls os_create_task_with_stack with http_server_task_main_loop as entry point, stack at DAT_800fceac, stack size 0x2000 (8KB), priority 0x18. TO ENABLE (TWO OPTIONS):
OPTION 1 -- Call cfg_http_firmware_upload_setup from NET_Subsystem_Init_Core: In NET_Subsystem_Init_Core (0x8009c1dc), before the call to NET_Start_All_Tasks, insert a JAL to cfg_http_firmware_upload_setup (0x80016598). Patch location: around 0x8009c220 (after HAL_Flash_Commit_PostProcess, before OS_Timer). Bytes: 3C190801 27390000 0320F809 00000000 (lui t9,0x8001; addiu t9,0x6598; jalr t9; nop) Adjust upper 16 bits to match actual address.
OPTION 2 -- Directly call os_create_task_with_stack from NET_Subsystem_Init_Core: This bypasses cfg_http_firmware_upload_setup and sets up the task directly. os_create_task_with_stack @ 0x80026b74 Task struct fields (from cfg_http_firmware_upload_setup decompile): local_20 = &DAT_800fceac (stack base) local_1c = &DAT_800c01d4 (stack limit / TCB?) local_18 = http_server_task_main_loop (0x80016518) local_14 = 0x18 (priority) local_10 = 0x2000 (stack size 8192 bytes)
BEHAVIOUR AFTER ENABLING: 1. http_stage_device_list() -- copies device list to staging buffer (one-time init) 2. Waits in os_msleep(10) loop until g_XBOX_WIFI_IFACE+0x24 (adapter IP) != 0 (HTTP only starts once the adapter has an IP address -- DHCP or static) 3. wlan_eapol_frame_dispatcher [Routes inbound EAPOL frames -- fully functional]
Called from the main RX path when EtherType 0x888E (EAPOL) is received. Gates on DAT_800c02d8 (EAPOL processing enabled flag) and frame type byte at +0x0E == 0x01. Looks up sending peer via wlan_peer_lookup_by_mac(src_mac). No peer entry -> drops frame silently.
Frame type routing (byte at param_1+0x0F): 0x00 -> dot1x_handle_key_exchange if subtype 0x02 and counter matches peer[0x0E] 0x01 -> eapol_pae_state_machine with state derived from peer[0x24]: peer[0x24] == 2 -> state 2 (identity request) peer[0x24] == 3 -> state 5 (failure) peer[0x24] == 4 -> state 2 peer[0x24] == 7 -> state 7 (key exchange ready) peer[0x24] == 8 -> state 8 0x02 -> eapol_pae_state_machine with state derived from peer[0x24]: peer[0x24] == 2 -> state 1 (success) peer[0x24] == 3 -> state 5 peer[0x24] == 4 -> state 1
This is FULLY FUNCTIONAL. The EAPOL frame exchange path works end to end. Only eapol_handle_key_exchange (0x800289BC) is stubbed out.

eapol_handle_key_exchange [WPA GAP 3 -- THE KEY EXCHANGE STUB] *** STUBBED OUT -- logs "EAP Failure" and returns ***
THIS IS THE ONLY MISSING PIECE for WPA. The surrounding infrastructure (state machine, frame dispatcher, peer lookup, port control) is ALL PRESENT and fully functional. Only this one function needs to be implemented.
Current implementation (3 instructions): wlan_eapol_frame_check(param_1, 0, 4, NULL) -- validates frame header only os_timer_cancel_and_clean(&DAT_800c3eb4, param_1+8) -- cleans up timer wlan_log_debug_info(2, "EAP Failure", ...) -- logs failure return -- EXITS WITHOUT DOING ANYTHING
REQUIRED IMPLEMENTATION: param_1 = EAPOL peer node struct pointer (wlan_node_t equivalent) param_1[1] = last received EAPOL frame pointer param_1[0xe] = state timer / retry counter param_1[0x11]= key available flag param_1[0x12]= port authorized flag
Step 1 -- Read ANonce from EAPOL message 1: p_frame = *(param_1+1) (last received frame) anonce[32] = p_frame + 0x1a (ANonce in EAPOL-Key frame at offset 26)
Step 2 -- Generate SNonce: RC4_KSA_Key_Schedule(local_state, random_seed, 32) Use first 32 bytes of keystream as SNonce (or use os_get_random_bytes if available)
Step 3 -- Derive PTK (PRF-512): Inputs: G_WPA_PMK (32 bytes), ANonce (32 bytes), SNonce (32 bytes), AP_MAC (6 bytes from p_frame+6), STA_MAC (6 bytes from g_NET_Interface_MAC_Table) Label: "Pairwise key expansion" Output: 64-byte PTK: PTK[0..15] = KCK (HMAC key for MIC verification) PTK[16..31] = KEK (AES key for GTK unwrap) PTK[32..47] = TK1 (temporal key bytes 0-15) PTK[48..63] = TK2 (temporal key bytes 16-31)
Step 4 -- Verify MIC on EAPOL message 3: mic_field = p_msg3 + 0x61 (MIC field at byte 97 of EAPOL-Key frame) Zero the MIC field in the frame buffer before computing computed_mic = HMAC-MD5(KCK, entire_msg3_frame) truncated to 16 bytes Compare computed_mic vs mic_field -- mismatch: call eapol_send_deauth_frame_cb, return
Step 5 -- Install PTK: ath_hal_set_key_cache_entry(key_slot=0, TK1+TK2, key_type=WPA_TKIP or CCMP)
Step 6 -- Extract and install GTK from message 3: gtk_wrapped = p_msg3 + 0x7F (GTK KDE in message 3) gtk = AES_unwrap(KEK, gtk_wrapped, gtk_len) ath_hal_set_key_cache_entry(key_slot=1, gtk, key_type=WPA_TKIP or CCMP)
Step 7 -- Send EAPOL message 4: eapol_send_packet(param_1) -- sends confirmation to AP
Step 8 -- Authorize port: param_1[0x12] = 1 (port authorized) dot1x_set_port_status(param_1, 1, ...) -- sets AUTHORIZED state
INFRASTRUCTURE ALREADY IN PLACE: wlan_eapol_frame_dispatcher @ 0x80028358 -- routes frames to this function eapol_pae_state_machine @ 0x800279F8 -- calls this at states 7/8 eapol_send_packet @ 0x80028944 -- sends EAPOL frames eapol_send_deauth_frame_cb @ 0x8009D0F8 -- sends deauth on failure dot1x_set_port_status -- controls port auth state RC4_KSA_Key_Schedule @ 0x8007CFEC -- available for PRF ath_hal_set_key_cache_entry -- installs keys in hardware

NET_Calculate_RFC1071_Checksum [Standard RFC 1071 Internet Checksum]
param_1 = pointer to data buffer (treated as ushort array) param_2 = length in DWORDs (function iterates param_2 * 2 shorts)
Algorithm (standard one's complement sum): sum = 0 for each ushort in buffer: sum += ushort if odd byte remains: sum += last_byte while sum >> 16: sum = (sum & 0xFFFF) + (sum >> 16) (fold carries) return sum & 0xFFFF (caller must complement to get final checksum)
NOTE: Caller is responsible for complementing the result (~uVar2 & 0xFFFF) before writing to XPP header Checksum field. This is standard RFC 1071 behaviour. The Ghidra decompiler auto-comment claiming this is non-standard is WRONG -- the NOT step is in the caller, not in this function.
Called from XPP packet builders to compute the XPP header checksum. Wire-verified correct against all captured XPP packets.

http_cgi_update_wifi_performance_params [CGI handler: sets HAL radio performance parameters]
Route: POST /cgi/config.cgi (WiFi performance sub-form) param_1 = ah (Atheros HAL context pointer) param_2 = form_payload_string (space-delimited token string from POST body)
Parses 7 space-separated decimal/hex values from form_payload_string via strtok_r: Token 1: ah+0x16B8 = tx_power or similar HAL param (raw ulong) Token 2: ah+0x16D8 = HAL param 2 (0xFFFFFFFF -> stored as 0) Token 3: ah+0x16DC = HAL param 3 Token 4: ah+0x1A80/0x1A82 = beacon interval (ushort, 0 or >0xFFFF -> 0x100 or 1000 depending on ah+0xDE4) Token 5: ah+0x170E = ushort param (0 or >0xFFFF -> 0x80) Token 6: ah+0x1710 = ushort param (0 or >0xFFFF -> 0x90) Token 7: ah+0x170C = ushort param (0 or >0xFFFF -> 0x100) Also sets: ah+0x1744 = 3 (flags register update marker)
These are low-level Atheros AR5212 HAL parameters controlling radio timing/performance. Clamping rules suggest: 0 = invalid (use default), >0xFFFF = invalid (use default). This handler exposes direct radio register manipulation through the web UI.

XPP_SHA1_Init_Modified [SHA1 context initialiser with non-standard 5th word]
Initialises a SHA_CTX with the standard RFC 3174 IV: h[0] = 0x67452301 h[1] = 0xEFCDAB89 h[2] = 0x98BADCFE h[3] = 0x10325476 h[4] = 0x00000000 <-- NON-STANDARD: standard SHA1 uses 0xC3D2E1F0 here Nl = 0
The zeroed h[4] makes this a modified SHA1, not compliant with standard SHA1. Used internally by the HMAC-SHA1 implementation for the XPP authentication path. The HMAC wrapper (xpp_calculate_hmac_sha1) calls this init then XPP_SHA1_Update.

RC4_Session_Rekey [Sets up a new RC4 session with freshly scheduled S-box, applies to two buffers]
Flow: 1. RC4_KSA_Key_Schedule(local_state, param_4, param_4_len) -- schedule new S-box 2. RC4_PRGA_Encrypt_Buffer(local_state, param_1, param_2, param_3) -- encrypt first buffer 3. os_release_driver_lock() / os_lock_network_mutex() -- lock swap mid-operation 4. RC4_KSA_Key_Schedule(second_state, param_3, ...) -- schedule second S-box 5. RC4_PRGA_Encrypt_Buffer(second_state, ...) -- encrypt second buffer (MIC or ICV) 6. RC4_PRGA_Encrypt_Buffer(second_state, puVar1, param_1, param_2) -- verify/finalise
The lock swap between steps 2 and 4 is notable -- the driver lock is released and the network mutex taken before the second KSA. This is the WEP per-packet encrypt path: IV+key -> KSA -> PRGA data -> PRGA ICV, with locking to prevent concurrent access to the shared RC4 state during the two-phase encrypt.

RC4_KSA_Key_Schedule [RC4 Key Scheduling Algorithm -- initialises S-box from key]
Standard RC4 KSA (RFC 4345 / Schneier): 1. Fills S-box with identity permutation: S[i] = i for i in 0..255 2. Scrambles S-box using key bytes: j = 0 for i in 0..255: j = (j + S[i] + key[i % keylen]) & 0xFF swap(S[i], S[j])
param_1 = output RC4 state struct (allocated by caller): +0x00: i counter (dword, starts 0) +0x04: j counter (dword, starts 0) +0x08: S-box (256 bytes) Total: 264 bytes
param_2 = key buffer pointer (byte array) param_3 = key length in bytes
Called by RC4_Session_Rekey before RC4_PRGA_Encrypt_Buffer. Used for WEP per-packet key mixing (IV + base key -> per-packet keystream). Also used internally by XPP_PBKDF2_F_Block HMAC path.

RC4_PRGA_Encrypt_Buffer [RC4 Pseudo-Random Generation Algorithm -- XOR keystream with data]
Standard RC4 PRGA: for n in 0..param_4: i = (i + 1) & 0xFF j = (j + S[i]) & 0xFF swap(S[i], S[j]) output[n] = input[n] XOR S[(S[i] + S[j]) & 0xFF]
param_1 = RC4 state struct (RC4_KSA_Key_Schedule output, 264 bytes) param_2 = output buffer (plaintext for encrypt, ciphertext for decrypt -- RC4 is symmetric) param_3 = input buffer param_4 = length in bytes to process
RC4 is symmetric so this function serves as both encrypt and decrypt. For WEP: called twice per packet -- once for data, once for ICV (CRC32 trailer). State struct is NOT reset between calls -- stream is continuous across both calls.

XPP_Negotiate_Security_Caps [802.11 association security capability negotiation]
Called during the association state machine when connecting to an AP. Probes hardware crypto acceleration via wlan_is_hw_accelerated_crypto() and XPP_Generate_Proprietary_Header() to determine which ciphers are usable.
Sets two capability flags in the BSS descriptor (iVar2): +0x10C: TKIP capable flag (set to 1 if TKIP hardware acceleration confirmed) +0x110: CCMP/AES capable flag (set to 1 if CCMP hardware acceleration confirmed)
Hardware OUI checks (iVar2+0xb8 / +0xdc): 0x027F0300 -> Atheros AR5212/AR5213 chipset 0x04F25000 -> Ralink chipset 0x02F25000 -> Realtek chipset
Association mode check (iVar2+0x14): 7 -> WPA/RSN mode: full TKIP+CCMP capability negotiation 0 -> open/WEP mode: checks param_1+0xEC8 for enc_type 3 or 6
The capability flags set here feed back into the handshake response builder to populate security_cap and cipher_cap bytes correctly for WPA operation. In stock firmware this is partially dead code since Gap 1 hardcodes 0x06/0x07.

WEP_KeyMix_And_ICV_Transform [WEP per-packet key mixing and ICV construction -- NOT standard RC4]
THIS IS NOT AN RC4 TRANSFORM despite the previous name. This implements the WEP per-packet key mixing algorithm (802.11 WEP key scheduling using the S-box lookup tables at DAT_800bb0bc and DAT_800bb2bc).
Algorithm (6-round Feistel-like structure on 5x16-bit state words + IV counter): Input: param_1 = output buffer (16 bytes: 4-byte header + 6x2-byte state words) param_2 = WEP base key (16 bytes: 13-byte WEP-128 key + 3 padding bytes) param_3 = per-packet state (10 bytes: 5x16-bit words + 1x16-bit IV counter offset) param_4 = IV sequence number (16-bit, packet counter)
S-box tables: DAT_800bb0bc = 512-byte low-byte substitution table (S[x & 0xFF]) DAT_800bb2bc = 512-byte high-byte substitution table (S[x >> 8])
6 forward rounds XOR each state word with S-box(prev_word XOR key_pair) 6 backward rounds apply 1-bit rotation mixing
Output format written to param_1: [0]: (param_4 >> 8) & 0xFF (IV high byte) [1]: ((param_4 >> 8) & 0x7F) | 0x20 (IV mid byte, bit 5 set, bit 7 clear per WEP spec) [2]: param_4 & 0xFF (IV low byte) [3]: partial XOR of final state (ICV seed byte) [4..15]: 6 state words little-endian (final mixed key material)
The IV byte layout [hi, hi&0x7F|0x20, lo] is standard WEP IV encoding. This produces the per-packet RC4 key: IV(3 bytes) + mixed_key(13 bytes) = 16 bytes. The output feeds RC4_KSA_Key_Schedule for the actual WEP keystream generation.

XPP_SME_Command_Worker [802.11 Station Management Entity -- drives auth/assoc state machine]
SME = Station Management Entity, the 802.11 connection state machine. Called when a pending association command is dequeued.
Guards (same as XPP_Reconnect_Timer_Callback): ath_hal_is_powered() != 0 AND sc_rc->assoc_flags & 0x13 != 0x13
When guards pass: Sets radio mode via wlan_hal_set_radio_mode(sc, 0x15) Sets sc_rc->assoc_flags |= 0x10 (radio mode set flag) Clears sc_rc->gap_1c_25[0..3] (sequence number / timing fields) Clears sc_bss+0x5C and +0x58 (BSS timing fields)
Then dispatches on assoc_flags: flags & 0x411 == 0x411 (auth+assoc+radio): -> WLAN_Build_Assoc_Request() beacon_interval = sc_nodeTable+0x48 timeout = ceil((gap_efa_10ff+0x1f6 + interval - 1) / interval) aligned to interval flags & 0x410 == 0x410 (auth+radio, no assoc yet): -> WLAN_Trigger_Auth_Assoc() param uVar5=0x15 (radio mode), uVar6=1 (trigger flag)
The 0x15 radio mode value corresponds to infrastructure STA mode with b/g rates.

XPP_Reconnect_Timer_Callback [Periodic reconnect watchdog, called from OS timer]
Checks two conditions before acting: 1. ath_hal_is_powered() != 0 (radio hardware is powered) 2. sc_rc->assoc_flags & 0x13 != 0x13 (NOT fully associated -- bits 0x01+0x02+0x10)
If both conditions met (radio on, not fully associated): XPP_Dispatch_Pending_Cmd() -- processes any queued XPP commands wlan_trigger_scan_sleep() -- triggers a background scan cycle
This implements the periodic reconnect polling. When the radio is powered but not associated (e.g. after losing the AP or after idle timeout), the firmware automatically retries connection via the pending command queue.
assoc_flags bit meanings (from XPP_SME_Command_Worker): bit 0x01 = auth completed bit 0x02 = assoc request sent bit 0x10 = radio mode set (wlan_hal_set_radio_mode called) bit 0x11 = auth+assoc requested -> WLAN_Build_Assoc_Request path bit 0x10 only -> WLAN_Trigger_Auth_Assoc path

XPP_Set_Connection_Mode [Copies NVRAM connection state into active runtime buffers]
Reads g_NVRAM_Conn_State and populates runtime connection fields: g_STATUS_WEP_Enabled = (ushort)NET_Interface_0_Gateway (WEP flag cast to short) g_WLAN_Retry_Countdown = decremented by 1 (pre-connect retry counter) g_XPP_Current_BSSID_Cache= g_NET_Interface_MAC_Table (6 bytes, current interface MAC) g_XPP_Conn_State = g_NVRAM_Conn_State
Connection mode dispatch: 0x01 -> memcpy(g_XPP_Target_ID_Buffer, G_WLAN_Active_SSID, 6) [SSID-based connect] 0x02 -> memcpy(g_XPP_Target_ID_Buffer, g_NVRAM_Target_BSSID, 6) [BSSID-based connect] sets g_XPP_Target_BSSID_Active = 1 0x03 -> memcpy(g_XPP_Target_ID_Buffer, g_CFG_Stored_Target_BSSID, 6) [stored BSSID]
Returns 1 always.

WLAN_RX_Frame_Decapsulate_And_Scan_Process [802.11 frame RX handler for scan result processing]
MISNAMED as XPP_Background_Scan_Thread -- this is NOT an XPP function. This is the 802.11 layer RX callback invoked when the Atheros HAL delivers a raw frame.
Flow: 1. Copies 6-byte source MAC from in_v1+0..5 into in_t9 (dest MAC buffer) 2. wlan_decapsulate_80211_to_ethernet() -- strips 802.11 header, returns Ethernet frame ptr Returns NULL on decap failure (bad FCS, unsupported frame type etc.) -> drops frame 3. wlan_copy_scan_result_channel_and_rssi() -- extracts channel + RSSI from 802.11 header Writes to g_WLAN_Scan_Channel_Table and g_WLAN_Scan_RSSI_Raw_Table at slot index Returns scan result slot ptr, or 0 if not a probe response/beacon 4. wlan_driver_ioctl_raw() -- issues HAL ioctl with slot+0xC/+0x10 params (updates HAL internal scan state machine) 5. net_spinlocked_write_ctx_2fields() -- updates interface stats under spinlock 6. NET_Process_Interface_Chain() -- pushes frame up the network stack for routing/XPP dispatch 7. os_spinlock_release() -- releases the HAL RX spinlock held by caller
Called from the HAL RX ISR path, not from a thread. os_spinlock_release() at end is mandatory -- the HAL holds the spinlock across this entire call.

WLAN_Build_Assoc_Request [802.11 association request builder]
Called from XPP_SME_Command_Worker when assoc_flags & 0x411 == 0x411. Guards against double-entry: if sc_bss+0x58 != 0 -> logs "busy" and returns.
On success: sc_bss+0x28 incremented (attempt count) sc_bss+0x58 = 8 (assoc pending marker) Calls wlan_send_assoc_req() with node capabilities from sc_nodeTable+0x1c timeout = interval-aligned value from gap_efa_10ff+0x1f6 / sc_nodeTable+0x48 On error: fires sc_bss+0x5ac+0x14 error callback if registered
Logging: "cservAssociate: Entered", "cservOp: %x cservState: %x", "cservAssociate: busy" NOTE: calls os_check_stack_canary() -- function does not return normally on stack overflow.

WLAN_Trigger_Auth_Assoc [802.11 authentication + association trigger]
Called from XPP_SME_Command_Worker when assoc_flags & 0x410 == 0x410 (radio set, no assoc yet). Guards: spinlock acquired. Checks sc_bss+0x58 == 0 (not already in progress).
On success: sc_bss+0x28 incremented (attempt count) sc_bss+0x58 = 0xC (auth+assoc pending marker)
Auth algorithm selection (uVar3 fed to wlan_retry_authentication): param_1[0x452] != 0 -> uVar3 = 0x80 (WPA/shared key path) param_1[0x3b9] == 0 AND sc_bss+0x5af+0x108 != 0 -> uVar3 = 1 (open system with capability bit) else -> uVar3 = 0 (standard open system)
Timeout from DAT_800c057c[sc_bss+0x60 * 4] * 100 (ms) Calls wlan_retry_authentication() with sc_nodeTable+0x1c as node target. Logging: "cservAuthAssoc: Entered", "cservOp: %x cservState: %x", "cservAuthAssoc: busy"

XPP_Network_Packet_Ready_Check [TLV parser timeout watchdog -- 10-tick stall recovery]
Increments XPP_Slot_Counter on each timer tick. When XPP_Slot_Counter reaches 10 (~1 second): Clears G_XPP_TLV_Parser_State = 0 (releases parser busy lock) Calls NET_Dequeue_And_Dispatch_Node() -- removes self from OS timer queue
G_XPP_TLV_Parser_State states: 0 = idle / ready for new connection 1 = TLV parse in progress (set at start of XPP_Type02_0x07_FlashConfig) 2 = TLV parse complete (set at end of XPP_Type02_0x07_FlashConfig)
While G_XPP_TLV_Parser_State != 0, XPP_Check_Auth_Status() returns 3 (busy). This watchdog ensures a stalled or abandoned parse (Xbox disconnected mid-config) cannot permanently block new XPP sessions. After 10 ticks state is force-cleared.

XPP_Check_Auth_Status [Returns current XPP authentication/pairing state]
Called from: XPP_Type02_0x01_Handshake (auth_status field), XPP_Type02_0x09_QueryStatus
Return values: 0 -> Paired and connected (g_XPP_Paired_Flag==1 and wlan_get_connection_readiness==0) 1 -> WLAN active but MAC mismatch (wlan_get_connection_readiness==1) 2 -> Idle, uptime > 400 ticks, not parsing TLV 3 -> TLV parser busy (G_XPP_TLV_Parser_State==1 or ==2), or uptime < 400 ticks (boot gate)
Pairing check: CRYPTO_Get_Hardware_ID() gets current hardware ID into local buffer. wlan_mac_addr_equal() compares against g_NET_Interface_MAC_Table. Match + wlan_get_connection_readiness==0 -> sets g_XPP_Paired_Flag=1. Mismatch + wlan_active -> clears g_XPP_Paired_Flag=0.
Boot gate: g_UPTIME_TICKS < 400 returns 3 regardless of pairing state. This prevents the adapter responding to handshakes during the first ~2 seconds after power-on.

XPP_Get_Channel_Or_Fallback Returns the current channel number for use in handshake byte 217 and Tag 0x05 responses.
Logic: XPP_Check_Auth_Status() == 0 (paired+connected): Returns wlan_freq_to_channel_number(0) -- live channel from radio hardware, masked to 8 bits. Otherwise: Returns g_CFG_Saved_Channel -- last configured channel stored in NVRAM. Initialised to 0x0B (channel 11) on factory reset. Written by Tag 0x84 in Type 0x07 CONNECT_REQ (clamped to hw EEPROM regional range).
This is the single source of truth for the channel field in both the handshake response and ADAPTER_INFO_RESP Tag 0x05.

XPP_Get_Link_State_Bitmask [Returns Tag 0x08 auth type value for ADAPTER_INFO_RESP]
Reads NET_Interface_0_Gateway (WEP/auth state flag, NOT the IP gateway): 0x00 -> returns 0x02 (open network / no WEP active) 0x01 -> returns 0x04 (WEP active, any key length) other-> returns 0x00 (undefined state)
Return value feeds xpp_select_best_security_mode() as param_1 on the dashboard. Combined with Tag 0x09 cipher echo to determine enc_type (1=Open, 2=WEP64, 3=WEP128, 4=WPA). For WPA: 0x10 or 0x20 required here, not produced by stock firmware (WPA Gap 3).

XPP_Tag_09_Handler_Get_Link_State [Returns Tag 0x09 / handshake trailer link_state value]
Reads g_WLAN_LinkActive and g_WLAN_LinkState_Bitmask (both set by XPP_Set_Link_State).
Return values (wire-verified): 0x01 -> no link / disassociated (g_WLAN_LinkActive == 0, or bitmask not 5 or 0x0D) 0x02 -> infrastructure linked (g_WLAN_LinkActive == 1 AND g_WLAN_LinkState_Bitmask == 5) 0x04 -> ad-hoc linked (g_WLAN_LinkActive == 1 AND g_WLAN_LinkState_Bitmask == 0x0D)
Used in: XPP_Type02_0x01_Handshake -> handshake trailer byte 1 (link_state) XPP_Type02_Build_AdapterInfo_Response -> Tag 0x09 response value

XPP_Set_Link_State [Tag 0x09 write handler in Type 0x07 CONNECT_REQ]
param_1: link state byte from Tag 0x09 0x01 -> DISASSOCIATE/IDLE: g_WLAN_LinkActive = 0 CFG_Set_WEP_Enabled(0x02) [WEP disabled] 0x02 -> INFRASTRUCTURE CONNECT: g_WLAN_LinkActive = 1 g_WLAN_LinkState_Bitmask = 5 [infra mode] CFG_Set_WEP_Enabled(0x04) [WEP enabled / connection active] 0x04 -> AD-HOC CONNECT: g_WLAN_LinkActive = 1 g_WLAN_LinkState_Bitmask = 0x0D [adhoc mode] CFG_Set_WEP_Enabled(0x04) other -> no-op, silently ignored
g_WLAN_LinkState_Bitmask values feed XPP_Tag_09_Handler_Get_Link_State(): 5 -> returns 0x02 (infrastructure linked) 0x0D -> returns 0x04 (ad-hoc linked)

CFG_Set_XPP_Auth_Mode [Tag 0x11 write handler in Type 0x07 CONNECT_REQ]
Sets g_XPP_Auth_Mode_Enabled based on param_1. Only 0x00 and 0x02 are processed -- all other values silently ignored. 0x00 -> g_XPP_Auth_Mode_Enabled = 0 (Tag 0x11 reports 0x00 = link not active) 0x02 -> g_XPP_Auth_Mode_Enabled = 1 (Tag 0x11 reports 0x02 = link active / encryption on)
This is the NVRAM-side encryption flag, distinct from the live HAL state. Wire-verified: 0x02 sent in all WEP CONNECT_REQ, 0x00 sent for open networks. Tags 0x08/0x09 report NVRAM-configured state. Tag 0x11 reports this HAL state. They can differ mid-association.

XPP_Get_RadioMode_Cap_Stub Writes 0x00 to param_1 (one byte). Called during handshake build -- clears the first byte of the IP telemetry block at payload offset 176+ (channel_bitmask_24ghz / extended bitmask region). Stock firmware sets the 2.4GHz channel bitmask to 0x00000FFE (channels 1-11, FCC) via a separate path. This stub only zeros the first byte of that region. Not a true stub -- it is the correct minimal implementation for the stock firmware.

XPP_Get_CipherCap_Stub_Returns0x07_WPA_GAP1 *** WPA GAP 1 -- companion stub to XPP_Get_SecurityCap_Stub_Returns0x06_WPA_GAP1 ***
Returns hardcoded 0x07 always. Written to XPP_Handshake_Response_Payload.cipher_cap (byte 175).
0x07 = bits 0x01+0x02+0x04 set = Open+WEP64+WEP128 shown, no WPA cipher bits. Bits 0x08 (CCMP), 0x10 (WPA2-TKIP), 0x20 (WPA2-CCMP) all CLEAR. The three low bits (0x01+0x02+0x04) MUST all be set or the entire handshake is rejected by the dashboard, so 0x07 is the minimum safe value.
FIX for WPA-TKIP: change to 0x0F (adds bit 0x08 CCMP) FIX for WPA2: change to 0x37 (adds bits 0x08+0x10+0x20) Must be combined with the security_cap fix (byte 174 -> 0x16) to have any effect.

WPA GAP 1 PATCH: change 0x6 to 0x16 to set bit 0x10 (WPA1/RSN capable) Bytes: 34030006 -> 34030016 (ori v1,zero,6 -> ori v1,zero,0x16) Also update byte 252 source (sec_cap_default) -- same stub, same fix required there

XPP_Get_SecurityCap_Stub_Returns0x06_WPA_GAP1 *** WPA GAP 1 -- hardcoded return prevents WPA PSK UI appearing on Xbox dashboard ***
Returns 0x06. Written to XPP_Handshake_Response_Payload.security_cap (byte 174).
v56 CORRECTION -- TWO SEPARATE DASHBOARD FUNCTIONS use bytes 174/175 vs 252/253: xpp_fetch_adapter_wpa_caps() processes bytes 174 + 175 for REJECTION logic: Masks byte174 to bits 0x02|0x04|0x10|0x20 Masks byte175 to low 6 bits Rejects if byte175 bits 0x01+0x02+0x04 not ALL set Rejects if byte174 has 0x20 set without 0x10 Stores byte174 & 0x10 -> AutoClass1+0xD70 (cap_wpa1_rsn) Stores byte174 & 0x20 -> AutoClass1+0xD74 (cap_wpa2_agn) xpp_select_best_security_mode() reads bytes 252 + 253 for UI SELECTION: param_1 = byte252 (sec_cap_default, same encoding as byte174) param_2 = byte253 (cipher_cap_default, same encoding as byte175) Produces enc_type (1=Open, 2=WEP64, 3=WEP128, 4=WPA) -> AutoClass1+0xE2E
cap_wpa1_rsn (AutoClass1+0xD70, from byte174 bit 0x10) must be non-zero AND byte252 must have bit 0x10 or 0x20 set for WPA path to activate. Both conditions required -- fixing only byte174 is not sufficient alone.
FIX: Change return from 0x06 to 0x16 (adds bit 0x10 to byte174). Also update byte252 (sec_cap_default) to 0x16 for the UI selection path. Patch: 8009914C li v0, 6 -> li v0, 0x16

XPP_Get_RadioMode_Cap_Hardcoded_0x05 Returns hardcoded 0x05 always. Written to XPP_Handshake_Response_Payload.radio_mode_cap (byte 208).
0x05 = bit0 (802.11b capable) + bit2 (ad-hoc capable). bit1 (802.11g capable) is CLEAR despite MN-740 being a b/g adapter. High bits 0xF8 MUST be zero or the dashboard rejects the entire handshake. This is intentional firmware behaviour -- the g-capability bit is suppressed.
XPP Main Dispatcher (TYPE 02) Handles Handshake, Scan, Init, and Config commands.

XPP_Type02_0x01_Handshake [Handles inbound Type 0x01, builds and sends Type 0x02 HANDSHAKE_RESPONSE]
DASHBOARD VALIDATION REQUIREMENTS (from xonlinedash_xbe.c decompile -- v56): The adapter MUST produce output that satisfies ALL of these checks in order: 1. total_frame_len == 0x11A (282 bytes exactly) or SILENT DISCARD before any field read 2. Copyright string at payload+20 compared as 21 x 4-byte dwords (84 bytes full compare) THIS IS CHECKED BEFORE HMAC -- mismatch discards before HMAC is even attempted 3. xpp_fetch_adapter_wpa_caps() validates bytes 174 + 175: byte175 bits 0x01+0x02+0x04 ALL must be set or reject byte174: bit 0x20 set without bit 0x10 set -> reject 4. HMAC-SHA1 20-byte compare (5 x 4-byte dwords, ALL must match) Ghidra auto-comment claiming "first 16 bytes" is WRONG -- all 20 bytes verified 5. xpp_select_best_security_mode() reads bytes 252+253 (NOT 174+175) to determine enc_type and pre-selected UI security mode
FIRMWARE SIDE -- what this function produces: Payload build order: +0x00 (offset 0): 20-byte HMAC-SHA1 Key: g_XPP_HMAC_Key (ROM, 16 bytes: cb275ff238ab61dc8799fa01ad17745e) Input: nonce(16 from Type 0x01) + adapter_MAC(6) + g_XPP_HMAC_MASTER_KEY(117) = 139 bytes +0x14 (offset 20): SEC_AUTH_COPYRIGHT_POEM (84 bytes, null-padded) "Device is Xbox Compatible. Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. All Rights Reserved." +0x68 (offset 104): model_name (32 bytes, null-padded) "Xbox Wireless Adapter (MN-740)" +0x88 (offset 136): fw_version_string (32 bytes) e.g. "1.0.2.26 Boot: 1.3.0.06" +0xA8 (offset 168): BSSID (6 bytes) or zeros +0xAE (offset 174): security_cap = XPP_Get_SecurityCap_Stub_Returns0x06_WPA_GAP1() MUST have bits 0x01+0x02+0x04 in byte175 set or dashboard rejects SET bit 0x10 here (0x16) to unlock WPA PSK UI +0xAF (offset 175): cipher_cap = XPP_Get_CipherCap_Stub_Returns0x07_WPA_GAP1() +0xB0 (offset 176): channel_bitmask_24ghz (4 bytes, FCC=0x00000FFE) +0xC0 (offset 192): channel_bitmask_ext (28 bytes, stock=zeros) +0xDC (offset 220): radio_mode_cap (byte208) = XPP_Get_RadioMode_Cap_Hardcoded_0x05() +0xDD (offset 221): dhcp_state (byte209) +0xDE (offset 222): ip_address (4 bytes, byte210-213) +0xE2 (offset 226): radio_active_214 +0xE3 (offset 227): auth_status_215 +0xE4 (offset 228): radio_active_guard (byte216) -- 0x02+ = ENTIRE HANDSHAKE REJECTED +0xE5 (offset 229): current_channel via XPP_Get_Channel_Or_Fallback() +0xE6 (offset 230): auth_algorithm (byte218) -- 0x03+ = ENTIRE HANDSHAKE REJECTED +0xE7 (offset 231): ssid_length +0xE8 (offset 232): ssid[32] +0x108(offset 252): sec_cap_default (byte252) -- feeds xpp_select_best_security_mode param_1 +0x109(offset 253): cipher_cap_default (byte253) -- feeds xpp_select_best_security_mode param_2 +0x10A(offset 254): reserved 0x0000 Trailer (4 bytes after payload): opmode_mask = XPP_Get_Link_State_Bitmask() link_state = XPP_Tag_09_Handler_Get_Link_State() reserved x2 = 0x00 0x00 Len_Dwords = 0x43, checksum over 0x43*4=268 bytes

XPP_Build_Type04_NetworkList_Response [Builds and sends Type 0x04 NETWORKS_LIST_RESPONSE]
Called asynchronously after scan completes via XPP_NetworkList_Manager_Loop.
v56 CORRECTION: Internal scan entry slot size is 0xB4 bytes (not 61 bytes). The 61-byte wire format (XPP_Network_Slot) is a COMPRESSED version. Internal storage: AutoClass1+0x78, 16 slots x 0xB4 bytes = 0x2D0 dwords (2880 bytes). Zeroed as 0x2D0 dwords before each NETWORKS_RESP by the dashboard on receive. Wire format is built by extracting fields from these 0xB4 internal slots.
STALE CACHE BEHAVIOUR (firmware-verified): xpp_refresh_active_scan_results() returns 0 networks: Falls back to g_Scan_Results_Backup (last successful scan). Adapter NEVER sends an empty list. Count > 0: saves to g_Scan_Results_Backup, caps at 16.
Wire slot build (61 bytes per slot, XPP_Network_Slot): bssid[6]: g_WLAN_Scan_BSSID_Table[slot * 0x48] privacy_flags: derived from g_WLAN_Scan_PrivacyFlags_Table -- MUST be 0 or 1 only (dashboard guard: value > 1 = ENTIRE response discarded) ssid_length: strlen() of scan entry SSID ssid[32]: scan entry SSID null-padded network_mode: g_WLAN_Scan_NetworkMode_Table[slot * 0x48] -- MUST be <= 2 channel: g_WLAN_Scan_Channel_Table[slot * 0x48] security_status: g_WLAN_Scan_SecurityStatus_Table[slot * 0x48] rate_indicator: g_WLAN_Scan_RateIndicator_Table[slot * 0x48] signal_rssi: g_WLAN_Scan_RSSI_Raw_Table[slot * 0x48] - 0x5F (subtract 95) supported_rates[8]: from g_WLAN_Scan_RateTable[rate_idx + slot * 0x48] pad[8]: zeros
body_size_dwords = ceil(0xD + count * 0x3D, 4) / 4 Checksum over body_size_dwords * 2 words.

XPP_NetworkList_Manager_Loop [Async scan state machine, timer-driven]
Called repeatedly by OS_Timer after XPP_Type02_0x03_WifiScan schedules it. Implements a two-phase scan with a 9-tick timeout (~900ms at 100ms/tick).
Phase 1 (g_XPP_Is_Scanning_Busy == 0): Sets g_XPP_Is_Scanning_Busy = 1 Calls HAL_WLAN_Trigger_Scan() to start hardware scan
Phase 2 (g_XPP_Is_Scanning_Busy == 1, subsequent timer ticks): Increments g_XPP_Scan_Tick_Count Calls HAL_WLAN_Get_Scan_State(): Returns non-zero = scan complete If scan complete OR tick count reaches 9 (timeout): NET_Dequeue_And_Dispatch_Node() -- removes self from timer queue g_XPP_Is_Scanning_Busy = 0 XPP_Build_Type04_NetworkList_Response() -- sends Type 0x04 to Xbox Frees the original request packet descriptor Resets g_XPP_Scan_Tick_Count = 0
Scan takes 50-900ms. A second Type 0x03 arriving while scanning is silently dropped in XPP_Type02_0x03_WifiScan (busy check). Maximum 9 timer ticks.

XPP_Type02_0x03_WifiScan [Handles inbound Type 0x03 NETWORKS_LIST_REQUEST]
Acquires spinlock, frees the inbound packet descriptor, releases lock. If g_XPP_Is_Scanning_Busy != 1: increments scan request counter at param_1+0x28, then schedules XPP_NetworkList_Manager_Loop via OS_Timer with XPP_Timer_Label_ScanCheck. If scan already in progress: request is SILENTLY DROPPED (no response, no error). Scan takes 50-900ms depending on channel count. Response is sent asynchronously from XPP_Build_Type04_NetworkList_Response when scan completes.

XPP_Type02_Build_AdapterInfo_Response [Handles Type 0x05 ADAPTER_INFO_REQUEST, builds Type 0x06 ADAPTER_INFO_RESPONSE]
Reads the tag list from the Type 0x05 request (count byte at iVar9+0xC, pairs starting at iVar9+0xD). Iterates each [tag][hint] pair and appends [tag][len][value] TLV to response payload. Tags with no data are silently omitted (sliding TLV behaviour). WRITE-ONLY tags (0x0A-0x0D, 0x0F, 0x10): corrupt the response byte -- they have no read handler. The bad-tag path at LAB_8009a918 does: *(pPayload+2)-- (decrements a stale byte). Avoid these.
Response prefix: 0x00 (firmware artifact) + echo of request tag count
Tag read handlers confirmed from decompile: 0x01 -> [tag=1][len=4][CFG_Device_IP 4 bytes] -- omitted if IP=0 0x02 -> [tag=2][len=1][dhcp_state] g_NET_InterfaceStatus==0 && g_DHCP_Interface_States==0x52 -> 0x01 (DHCP acquired) g_NET_InterfaceStatus==0 && other -> 0x00 (no DHCP) g_NET_InterfaceStatus==1 -> 0x02 (static/manual) 0x04 -> [tag=4][len=1][wlan_is_radio_active()] 0x00=off 0x01=on(single) 0x02=on(b+g) 0x05 -> [tag=5][len=1][XPP_Get_Channel_Or_Fallback()] 0x06 -> [tag=6][len=6][wlan_get_current_bssid() 6 bytes] 0x07 -> [tag=7][len=ssid_len][ssid string] 0x08 -> [tag=8][len=1][XPP_Get_Link_State_Bitmask()] 0x09 -> [tag=9][len=1][XPP_Tag_09_Handler_Get_Link_State()] 0x0E -> [tag=14][len=1][CFG_Get_Target_Channel()] 0x11 -> [tag=17][len=1][wlan_get_encryption_type()] 0x81 -> [tag=129][len=6][g_NET_Interface_MAC_Table 6 bytes] 0x82 -> [tag=130][len=1][regulatory_domain from ath_hal_get_hw_info()] 0x83 -> [tag=131][len=1][g_CFG_Reconnect_Mode] 0x84 -> [tag=132][len=1][g_CFG_Saved_Channel] 0x85 -> [tag=133][len=1][g_CFG_TX_Rate_Index] 0x86-0x89 -> [tag][len=0xFF][512 bytes EEPROM block from G_XPP_Debug_Buffer] Radio MUST be off (tag 0x04 = 0x00) or returns 0xFF-filled block

XPP_Type02_0x07_FlashConfig [Handles inbound Type 0x07 CONNECT_TO_SSID_REQUEST]
Parses the TLV stream from the Xbox. Tags processed in order (forward pass, no backtrack). Unknown tag -> logs "got_unknown %d" -> ABORTS parse loop (all subsequent tags dropped). Sets G_XPP_TLV_Parser_State = 2 on loop exit. Sends Type 0x08 CONNECT_RESPONSE with result 0x00 on success.
TLV tag dispatch (verified from decompile): 0x00 -> Flash_Commit_Settings() + CFG_Save_To_Flash() + hw_trigger_reboot_sequence() 0x01 -> memcpy(&CFG_Device_IP, payload, 4) 0x02 -> g_NET_InterfaceStatus = (byte == 2) ? 1 : 0 0x03 -> memset+memcpy to g_NVRAM_User_Settings.Legacy_Padding (admin_id, max 16+NUL=17 bytes) 0x04 -> WLAN_Set_Operating_Mode(byte) 0x05 -> CFG_Set_Max_Channel(byte) 0x06 -> CFG_Set_Paired_Xbox_MAC(payload[6]) 0x07 -> CFG_Set_Target_SSID(payload, len) 0x08 -> CFG_Set_WEP_Enabled(byte) 0x09 -> XPP_Set_Link_State(byte) [0x01=idle 0x02=infra 0x04=adhoc] 0x0A -> Wifi_Set_Security_Key(payload, slot=0) [5 bytes WEP-40] 0x0B -> Wifi_Set_Security_Key(payload, slot=1) 0x0C -> Wifi_Set_Security_Key(payload, slot=2) 0x0D -> Wifi_Set_Security_Key(payload, slot=3) 0x0E -> CFG_Set_Target_Channel(byte) 0x0F -> CFG_Set_WEP128_Key_Slot x4 slots [13 bytes each] 0x10 -> STUB: advances pointer only, PMK (32 bytes) DISCARDED -- WPA Gap 2 0x11 -> CFG_Set_XPP_Auth_Mode(byte) [0x00=no enc, 0x02=enc active, others ignored] 0x12 -> NOT PRESENT: falls to default -> logs "got_unknown" -> ABORTS PARSE LOOP 0x81 -> XPP_Establish_Secure_Identity_Link(payload[6]) 0x82 -> NET_Interface_Reset_And_Reconnect(0, byte, hw_mac) 0x83 -> g_CFG_Reconnect_Mode = byte [0/1/2, clamped to 1 if invalid] 0x84 -> g_CFG_Saved_Channel = byte [clamped to 0x0B if outside hw EEPROM range] 0x85 -> g_CFG_TX_Rate_Index = byte [whitelist validated: 0/2/4/0xB/0xC/0x12/0x18/0x24/0x30/0x48/0x60/0x6C only]
TLV tag dispatch jump table (tags 0x00-0x10). Tag index = v1, table at 0x800AA464

Secondary dispatch: tag >= 0x11. Adjusts v1 relative to 0x11. v1 -= 0x11: if 0 -> Tag 0x11 handler (0x8009B000) v1 -= 0x70: if 0 -> Tag 0x81 handler (0x8009AB0C) v1 -= 0x01: if 0 -> Tag 0x82 handler (0x8009AB38) else -> default (0x8009B038) -- unknown tag, PARSE ABORT
WPA GAP 2b PATCH POINT: add beq for Tag 0x12 between Tag 0x11 check and Tag 0x81 check. After the beq v1,zero -> Tag0x11_handler at 0x8009AAB8: addiu v1, v1, -1 ; check for Tag 0x12 beq v1, zero, TAG_0x12 ; branch to new passphrase handler nop This requires shifting or replacing the subsequent instructions.
v1 == 0 means tag was 0x11 -> Tag 0x11 handler (CFG_Set_XPP_Auth_Mode) WPA PATCH: insert Tag 0x12 check immediately after this beq instruction

TAG 0x10 HANDLER -- WPA PMK STUB (WPA GAP 2a) Current: addiu s0,s0,0x20 -- advances parse pointer by 32 bytes, PMK DISCARDED FIX PATCH: replace with call to store PMK: lui a0, HIGH(G_WPA_PMK) ; destination buffer (allocate ~0x20 bytes in NVRAM) addiu a0, a0, LOW(G_WPA_PMK) or a1, s0, zero ; source = current TLV payload pointer ori a2, zero, 0x20 ; length = 32 bytes jal memcpy nop lui at, HIGH(G_WPA_PMK_Ready) ori v1, zero, 1 sb v1, LOW(G_WPA_PMK_Ready)(at) ; set ready flag addiu s0, s0, 0x20 ; advance pointer (keep this) j 0x8009b078 ; continue TLV loop (was falling through) nop Total: ~12 instructions. Need ~48 bytes of free space or a trampoline.
TAG 0x10: j 0x8009b078 -- continues TLV loop after discarding PMK With patch: this jump should be kept but preceded by PMK storage code

DEFAULT HANDLER -- unknown tag path (WPA GAP 2b) ALL unrecognised tags including Tag 0x12 (WPA passphrase) arrive here. Calls wlan_log_debug_info with "got_unknown" string then jumps to 0x8009b06c which sets v1 = -1 and jumps to 0x8009b120 (function exit) -- ABORTS ENTIRE PARSE LOOP. Any tags after the unknown tag in the same packet are silently dropped.
PATCH FOR TAG 0x12 (WPA passphrase, 8-63 bytes): At 0x8009AEB8 in the secondary dispatch (tags >= 0x11): After the check for tag 0x11 at 0x8009AAB8: addiu v1, v1, -0x70 (adjust to 0x11 base) beq v1, zero -> 0x8009B000 (Tag 0x11 handler, already correct) addiu v1, v1, -0x1 (check for 0x12) beq v1, zero -> TAG_0x12_HANDLER (new branch needed here) j 0x8009B038 (default -- unknown)
TAG_0x12_HANDLER (new code, needs free space or trampoline): -- s1 = tag length (already loaded) -- s0 = payload pointer (already positioned) Validate: length >= 8 AND length <= 0x3F (63) or jump to default lui a0, HIGH(G_WPA_Passphrase) addiu a0, a0, LOW(G_WPA_Passphrase) or a1, s0, zero ; source or a2, s1, zero ; length (s1 already has TLV length byte) jal memcpy nop lui at, HIGH(G_WPA_Pass_Len) sb s1, LOW(G_WPA_Pass_Len)(at) lui at, HIGH(G_WPA_PBKDF2_Pending) ori v1, zero, 1 sb v1, LOW(G_WPA_PBKDF2_Pending)(at) ; schedule PBKDF2 in worker task addu s0, s0, s1 ; advance pointer by length j 0x8009b078 ; continue TLV loop nop Total: ~20 instructions. PBKDF2 must run in worker task not inline (takes 100-200ms)

XPP_Type02_0x09_QueryStatus [Handles Type 0x09 BEACON_REQUEST, sends Type 0x0A BEACON_RESPONSE]
Sent by Xbox every 1 second. 5-second beacon loss -> standby. 30-second watchdog -> radio off.
RSSI SMOOTHING CORRECTIONS (v56, from xonlinedash_xbe.c decompile): The -91 dBm guard is in xpp_handle_beacon_response (dashboard side), NOT in the 5-sample averager. It applies ONLY when link_state == 0x00. Guard: rssi > -91 dBm or frame discarded.
link_state -> RSSI handling: 0x00 (authenticated): real RSSI stored in circular buffer IF rssi > -91 dBm if rssi <= -91 dBm: entire beacon response discarded 0x01 (associating): RSSI buffer slot forced to 0x80 (not 0xBA as previously stated) 0xBA is the seed for the SMOOTHED OUTPUT, not the per-slot value 0x02 (open/idle): RSSI buffer slot forced to 0xA6 -- DOES contribute to average (NOT excluded from average as v55 implied) 0x03 (WEP in progress): sets this+0x5c = 0xFF (early-trigger flag) does NOT reset circular buffer index (buffer continues)
Smoothed output = 0x80 when NO link_state==0x00 sample exists in the 5-sample window. The 0x80 value means "no valid measurement yet", not a specific RSSI reading.
Dashboard signal bar thresholds applied to smoothed_rssi byte: rssi <= -91 dBm: 0 bars (entire response discarded) rssi <= -82: 1 bar rssi <= -72: 2 bars rssi <= -68: 3 bars rssi <= -58: 4 bars rssi > -58: 5 bars (excellent)
Response payload (XPP_Beacon_Response_Payload, 4 bytes): [0] auth_status = XPP_Check_Auth_Status() [1] smoothed_rssi= drvr_get_smoothed_rssi() -- 5-sample avg, firmware-scaled [2] tx_rate_code = drvr_get_tx_rate_code() & 0x7F [3] reserved = 0x00 NOTE: 16 bytes of uninitialised memory follow the 4-byte payload in wire frames -- NOT protocol.
Len_Dwords = 0x04. Total frame = 30 bytes (14 Eth + 12 XPP + 4 payload).

xpp_calculate_hmac_sha1 [Standard RFC 2104 HMAC-SHA1 -- NOT modified]
THIS IS STANDARD HMAC-SHA1. The modified SHA1 init (h[4]=0) seen in XPP_SHA1_Init_Modified is a DIFFERENT function used elsewhere. This function uses correct RFC 3174 SHA1 throughout.
RFC 2104 HMAC construction (confirmed from decompile): ipad = key XOR 0x36 (padded to 64 bytes) opad = key XOR 0x5c (padded to 64 bytes) inner = SHA1(ipad || message) outer = SHA1(opad || inner)
param_1 = message buffer pointer (the 139-byte input for XPP auth) param_2 = message length in bytes param_3 = output digest destination (in the XPP payload buffer) param_4 = max digest bytes to copy (normally 0x14 = 20 bytes, but clamped: min(param_4, 0x14)) in_t0 = key buffer pointer (g_XPP_HMAC_Key, 16 bytes: cb275ff238ab61dc8799fa01ad17745e) in_t1 = key length (16)
After computing the 20-byte digest: xpp_copy_digest_to_packet(digest_ptr, param_3, min(param_4, 0x14)) xpp_security_final_callback()
XPP Authentication input (139 bytes total): nonce[16] from Type 0x01 payload (random, per-session) adapter_MAC[6] from g_NET_Interface_MAC_Table master_key[117] g_XPP_HMAC_MASTER_KEY ROM string = 139 bytes -> SHA1 inner hash -> SHA1 outer hash -> 20-byte digest at payload[0..19]
Wire-verified: digest matches expected value for known nonce + MAC + master_key inputs.

BBN_Handle_Discovery_Task [Handles inbound BBN UDP discovery queries on port 42424]
Called from OS timer. Guards via g_BBN_Processing_Lock (non-reentrant).
One-time init: if g_BBN_Initialized_Flag == 0: WLAN_RX_Frame_Decapsulate_And_Process() -- ensures RX path is ready Sets g_BBN_Initialized_Flag = 1
Query validation (20-byte packet): Reads from buf_BBN_Incoming_Request via xpp_session_recv_metadata(g_BBN_Socket_RX) iVar6 != 0x14 (not exactly 20 bytes) -> logs "not_a_discovery_request_err", drops First 4 bytes != 0x50000000 -> logs "packetId_error", drops
Response construction (126 bytes into buf_BBN_Outgoing_Response): [0x00] 0x51000000 type marker [0x04] G_BBN_PROTO_VERSION [0x08] 0x01000000 if NVRAM==defaults, else 0x00000000 (factory_default_flag) [0x0C] str_BBN_Device_Name (32 bytes, "MN-740 Bridge") [0x2C] str_BBN_Model_Info (32 bytes, "MN-740") [0x38] CFG_Device_IP (4 bytes big-endian) [0x3C] 0x00000000 (reserved gap) [0x40] G_NET_ActiveSubnetMask [0x44] 0x00000000 (reserved gap) [0x48] G_NET_PrimaryDNS [0x4C] g_NET_Interface_MAC_Table (6 bytes adapter MAC) [0x54] nonce_echo: bytes 16-19 of incoming query copied verbatim [0x5A] 0x40070004 (hardcoded capability flags) Version fields byte-swapped (big-endian to wire): [0x5E] G_FW_MajorVersion >> 8 | << 8 [0x60] G_FW_MinorVersion [0x62] G_FW_Revision [0x64] G_FW_Build [0x66] G_HW_MajorVersion [0x68] G_HW_MinorVersion [0x6A] G_HW_FeatureFlags [0x6C] G_HW_RegionID
Sends 0x7E (126) bytes via udp_send_to_server() to broadcast 255.255.255.255:42424 from g_BBN_Socket_TX. Logs error if send returns != 126 bytes.

XPP_Secure_Config_Update [Auth callback for TFTP port 16932] Called by TFTP_Process_New_Request when a WRQ or RRQ arrives on port 16932. param_2 = raw UDP payload pointer (the 67-byte WRQ/RRQ packet body) tftp_op_mode: firmware-internal encoding, INVERTED from wire TFTP opcode: tftp_op_mode == 2 -> RRQ (wire opcode 1): NO AUTH, logs and returns immediately. tftp_op_mode == 1 -> WRQ (wire opcode 2): TWO auth checks performed:
CHECK 1 — MAC match (param_2[0x00..0x05]): Compared against g_NET_Interface_MAC_Table. Unpaired adapter: table holds adapter hardware MAC. Paired adapter: table holds paired Xbox console MAC (set by CFG_Set_Paired_Xbox_MAC). Failure -> logs "mac_error", returns.
CHECK 2 — HMAC-SHA1 (param_2[0x26..0x39], 20 bytes): Key: g_XPP_HMAC_Key (ROM constant, 16 bytes: cb275ff238ab61dc8799fa01ad17745e) Input: g_NVRAM_User_Settings.Legacy_Padding (admin_id, default "admin", max 16 chars) Expected digest stored at DAT_800cdfec after computation. Wire digest read from param_2+0x26 (20 bytes inside the TFTP filename field). Failure -> logs "password_error1", returns.
Both pass -> sets wlan_promiscuous(0x78), SYS_Set_Update_Mode(1), g_ACTIVE_IFACE_HANDLE=1. Default HMAC result for "admin": 822f85b7ca0cf6faad5f3c260430626d1b083ec8

XPP_Rebuild_Auth_Hash [Rebuilds the MAC address hash table for peer authentication]
Clears and rebuilds G_MAC_HASH_TABLE_BASE (256 entries, 0x100 bytes) and G_MAC_NODE_POOL (600 bytes, up to 100 entries of 6 bytes each MAC_Hash_Node).
For each entry in G_ATH_Hardware_Config_Struct (count in .seq_num_ack field): 1. Reads 6-byte MAC from .field5_0x14 + entry*6 2. Computes hash: (MAC[0:2] as ushort + upper byte of same) & 0x3F -> bucket index (0-63) 3. Inserts MAC_Hash_Node into bucket as linked list (chaining on collision)
This table is used by NET_Register_Peer_MAC() to fast-lookup whether a source MAC is a known/trusted peer. Called after factory reset, pairing changes, and interface reinitialisation to keep the hash table consistent with NVRAM state.

XPP_Check_Whitelist [MAC address peer authorisation -- hash table lookup with mode flip]
Checks if param_1 (6-byte MAC as 3x ushort) is in the trusted peer hash table built by XPP_Rebuild_Auth_Hash().
Hash function (bucket = 0-63): bucket = ((MAC[4:5] as ushort) + (MAC[4] as byte)) & 0x3F Walks linked list at G_MAC_HASH_TABLE_BASE[bucket * 4] Match: all 3 ushorts (6 bytes) must equal node entry
Return logic depends on G_ATH_Hardware_Config_Struct.header_template: header_template == 1 (ALLOW/whitelist mode): MAC found -> return 1 (authorised) MAC missing -> return 0 (rejected) header_template != 1 (DENY/blacklist mode): MAC found -> return 0 (rejected) MAC missing -> return 1 (authorised)
Short-circuit (always allow): conn_state._0_1_ == 0 (pairing not active) OR seq_num_ack == 0 (no entries in table) -> returns 1 unconditionally
Called via function pointer DAT_800c03f0 = XPP_Verify_Device_Authorized, registered in AUTH_GATE_XPP_Force_Xbox_Mode. This is the MAC-level gate for all inbound XPP packets after EtherType validation.
<- Fetching head of Hash Bucket

XPP_Verify_Device_Authorized [MAC whitelist gate -- registered as g_FnPtr_XPP_Verify_Device_Authorized]
Called on every inbound XPP packet before dispatch. param_1 = pointer to 6-byte source MAC from Ethernet frame header.
Fast-path: if G_ATH_Hardware_Config_Struct.conn_state._0_1_ == 0 (no active pairing): Returns 1 immediately (allow all -- open/factory state).
Normal path: Calls XPP_Check_Whitelist((short*)param_1) -- hash table MAC lookup. Return 1 (authorised): packet passed to XPP dispatcher. Return 0 (rejected): logs MAC address to WLAN debug (level 8): sprintf(buf, STR_MAC_FORMAT, mac[0], mac[1]) wlan_log_debug_info(8, STR_ERR_UNAUTHORIZED_PC, buf) Returns 0 -- packet silently dropped.

OS_ISR_Tick_And_Queue_Poll [Main ISR: tick counter increment + timer + queue check]
Called from hardware interrupt service routine on each system tick.
1. Increments G_OS_Tick_Counter (global uptime tick, used for RSSI timeouts etc.)
2. Handshake timeout check: G_XPP_Handshake_Timeout-- If reaches zero: sets DAT_800c0010=1, flags bit 0x01 for wakeup
3. Queue poll: Reads *G_Queue_Read_Ptr: If 0: advances read pointer (wraps at G_Queue_End_Ptr back to G_Queue_Start_Ptr) If non-zero: sets DAT_800c0018=1, flags bit 0x02 for wakeup
4. Wakeup dispatch: bit 0x02 set: increments DAT_800c0024, calls os_task_make_ready(-0x7fdb57ac) This wakes the main network task from blocking queue wait bit 0x01 set: calls os_timer_slice_yield_check() If slice expired: reloads G_XPP_Handshake_Timeout from task struct +0x18
G_XPP_Handshake_Timeout controls the 5-second beacon loss detection: Set to ~50 ticks (5 seconds at 100ms/tick) when beacon exchange is active. When it hits zero the adapter enters standby -- radio stays on but stops routing.

XPP_Establish_Secure_Identity_Link [Tag 0x81 handler -- registers Xbox MAC as trusted peer]
param: p_mac_addr -- 6-byte MAC address from Tag 0x81 payload in Type 0x07 CONNECT_REQ
Flow (spinlock protected): 1. Net_Init_Socket_Logic(p_mac_addr, 6) -- validates and registers MAC 2. If success: NET_Register_Peer_MAC(p_mac_addr) -- stores as trusted peer MAC 3. Sets g_XPP_Current_Session_ID = XPP_Get_Identity_Token() -- starts new auth session

xpp_check_firmware_update_status [Boot init: opens both TFTP sockets]
Called from net_main_task() as a fixed step during boot, before DHCP, before any Xbox connection. Opens both TFTP listening sockets: TFTP_Open_Port16932_Socket(XPP_Secure_Config_Update, xpp_tftp_commit_config) Port 16932 = paired port, MAC+HMAC auth on WRQ, no auth on RRQ. TFTP_Open_Port69_Socket(0, TFTP_VFS_WRQ_Completion_Callback) Port 69 = unpaired port, no auth on WRQ or RRQ.
Both sockets open at power-on but transfers are gated by g_XPP_Session_Handle == -1. Gate is set by TFTP_Session_Enable() during the Type 0x01/0x02 handshake. Without a prior successful XPP handshake, both ports respond with "Transfers currently disabled".

FUNCTION.NAME: TFTP_Session_Enable
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: TFTP_Session_Enable Sets g_XPP_Session_Handle = -1 (0xFFFFFFFF). Called during the XPP Type 0x01/0x02 handshake flow to gate-open both TFTP ports. Without this call any WRQ or RRQ on either port receives "Transfers currently disabled".

FUNCTION.NAME: TFTP_Session_Disable
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: TFTP_Session_Disable Sets g_XPP_Session_Handle = 0 (cleared). Called on XPP session teardown / watchdog timeout to close the TFTP gate. Any in-progress transfers receive no further service after this is called.

FUNCTION.NAME: TFTP_Process_New_Request
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT:
TFTP_Process_New_Request Main entry point for all incoming WRQ/RRQ packets on both port 69 and port 16932. param_4 == 0 -> port 69 path (no auth, g_XPP_Active_Frequency callback) param_4 == 1 -> port 16932 path (XPP_Secure_Config_Update auth callback)
Flow: 1. Rejects if g_TFTP_Session_Active_Flag >= 1 (one session at a time). 2. Validates opcode < 3 (1=RRQ, 2=WRQ only). 3. For port 16932: filename field starts at p_tftp_opcode+0x3d (binary auth blob, not text). For port 69: filename is a null-terminated string starting at p_tftp_opcode+2. 4. Lowercases the mode string. 5. Allocates TFTP_Transfer_State via TFTP_Session_Alloc (pool tag 0x18, 0x80 bytes). 6. Sets port_source_id: 0x45 (port 69) or 0x4224 (port 16932). 7. Checks g_XPP_Session_Handle == -1, else sends "Transfers currently disabled". 8. Dispatches auth callback — for RRQ on port 16932: callback returns immediately (no checks). For WRQ on port 16932: MAC check then HMAC-SHA1 check. auth fail return -1 -> "Access violation", return -2 -> silent drop. 9. Allocates ephemeral TID UDP socket via xpp_udp_open_or_bind_socket(). 10. RRQ: sets state=6 (SEND), block=1, opens VFS file, callback = g_XPP_Link_Quality. WRQ: sets state=1 (RECV), sends ACK block 0 immediately (RFC 1350), callback = g_XPP_Security_State.
State values written at offset 0x38 (state_flags_lo): 1 = RECV (WRQ - waiting for DATA blocks) 6 = SEND (RRQ - sending DATA blocks) 2 = SEND_RRQ (RRQ initial state before first block sent)

FUNCTION.NAME: xpp_tftp_process_ack
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT:
xpp_tftp_process_ack *** BUG: BLOCK COUNTER NEVER ADVANCES ON RRQ ***
This function handles incoming ACK packets from the client during RRQ (read/send) sessions.
THE BUG - two separate problems that compound each other:
PROBLEM 1 - Wrong field used for block number comparison: The ACK block number from the wire is read from: *(short *)(*(int *)(p_protocol_state + 0xc) + 2) This is: *(p_session->vfs_filename_ptr + 2) i.e. bytes 2-3 of the VFS FILENAME STRING, not any packet buffer. The filename pointer at 0x08 is being read as if it were a packet buffer pointer. This means the "received block number" is always two bytes into the filename string ("ma" for mac.dat, "r5" for ar5eepo.dat etc.) — garbage, never matching.
PROBLEM 2 - Block counter increment is AFTER the branch: *(short *)(p_protocol_state + 0x2c) = *(short *)(p_protocol_state + 0x2c) + 1 This line only executes if the block number comparison PASSES. Since the comparison always fails (Problem 1), next_expected_block NEVER increments.
RESULT: Every ACK received is treated as out-of-sequence: param_1->out_of_seq_count++ (the else branch always fires) State stays at 2 (SEND), xpp_tftp_send_data_block re-sends block 1 forever. Client gets the same block on every retry until retry_limit_countdown hits zero and the session is torn down with a timeout error.
WHY FIRMWARE FLASH WORKS: WRQ (write) path goes through xpp_tftp_data_handler, NOT this function. xpp_tftp_data_handler correctly reads the block number from param_2 (actual packet buffer pointer) and correctly increments next_expected_block on success. The bug is 100% isolated to the RRQ ACK handler.
AFFECTED FILES (all RRQ reads broken): dbgout.txt, ar5eepo.dat, ar5maco.dat, image (read-back)
UNAFFECTED: WRQ firmware flash (xpp_tftp_data_handler - correct implementation) WRQ virtual file writes (TFTP_VFS_WRQ_Completion_Callback - correct)
CORRECT IMPLEMENTATION SHOULD BE: *(short *)(*(int *)(p_protocol_state + 0x18) + 2) // packet buffer at 0x18 not: *(short *)(*(int *)(p_protocol_state + 0x0c) + 2) // filename ptr at 0x0c
FUNCTION.TYPEINFO_CMT: undefined __stdcall xpp_tftp_process_ack(int p_protocol_state, uint param_2, uint param_3, undefined4 param_4)

FUNCTION.NAME: xpp_signal_data_ready
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT:
xpp_signal_data_ready -- TFTP packet dispatcher (routes incoming packets to correct handler) Called when a UDP packet arrives on an active TFTP session socket.
Reads opcode from wire packet: *(short*)(session+0x0C dereference)+0 -> opcode opcode 3 (DATA) -> xpp_tftp_data_handler (WRQ receive path -- WORKS CORRECTLY) opcode 4 (ACK) -> xpp_tftp_process_ack (RRQ send path -- BROKEN, see below) opcode 5 (ERROR) -> xpp_tftp_handle_remote_error
NOTE -- the ACK dispatch at 80003200 passes ONLY a0=p_session to xpp_tftp_process_ack. The actual received packet buffer (t8, loaded at 8000315c from session+0x10) is in a2 for the DATA handler call (800031ec) but is NOT passed at 80003200 for the ACK call. This is the ROOT CAUSE of the RRQ bug -- xpp_tftp_process_ack receives no pointer to the incoming ACK packet and therefore cannot read the wire block number from it. It then reads from session+0x0C instead, which is garbage (client_ip field).
FIX at 80003200: change to or a2,t8,zero before the jal (pass t8 as param_2) AND fix xpp_tftp_process_ack to use param_2 instead of session+0x0C.
